name: Chapter 3: Thin vs deep book
description: The same market order against a thin book and a deep book.

lesson.title: Thin vs deep book
lesson.summary: Send the same order into a thin book and a deep book and compare what it costs and how far it moves the price. Depth, not value, decides price impact.

beats.title: A thin book
beats.text: This market is [b]thin[/b]: only 10 shares wait at each of the first few ask prices, and the next real size is far away at 102.00.

beats.title: A large buyer arrives
beats.text: Atlas Capital sends a market order to [b]buy 60 shares[/b].

wait.hint: Press Step until it starts trading (or Tick to run it all).

beats.title: It climbs the book
beats.text: To find 60 shares the order had to climb through every ask level, paying more at each one. The last price jumped from 100.10 to [b]102.00[/b].

beats.title: Same moment, deep book
beats.text: Now imagine the same company at the same moment, but a market maker keeps [b]500 shares at every price[/b]. This is a [b]deep[/b] book.

beats.title: The identical order
beats.text: Atlas Capital sends the identical order: [b]buy 60 at market[/b].

wait.hint: Press Step until it trades (or Tick).

beats.title: Depth decides the impact
beats.text:
In the deep book the whole order filled at the best price and the last price did not move. In the thin book the same order moved the price by almost [b]two full points[/b] and paid more for every share.

Price impact depends on depth, not on what the company is worth. A market with little real depth is easy to push around, which later chapters exploit.
